case.case_title: Weerawansa v. The Attorney-General and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, SC Application No. 730/96, decided on 26 June 2000

clause.text: No person shall be arrested except according to law and must be informed of the reason.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s arrest on 30.04.96 was in accordance with law and whether he was informed of the reason for arrest as required by Article 13(1).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner argued that his arrest was not based on reasonable suspicion of unlawful activity under section 6(1) of the PTA and thus was unlawful and violated Article 13(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents claimed the arrest was under section 6(1) of the PTA based on information and statements linking the petitioner to unlawful activity involving illegal importation of weapons and aircraft parts.
key_facts: The petitioner was arrested on 30.04.96 by CID officers claiming suspicion of unlawful activity under the PTA.
The arrest was based on a report dated 04.03.96 and statements by Hasheem, an arrested suspect.
The report and statements did not reasonably implicate the petitioner in unlawful activity under the PTA.
The petitioner was likely informed he was suspected of unlawful activity at arrest.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court held that arrest under Article 13(1) must be in accordance with procedure established by law, here section 6(1) of the PTA, which requires reasonable suspicion of unlawful activity. Mere assertion without credible material does not suffice. The petitioner’s arrest was not in accordance with law as no reasonable suspicion existed.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found the 2nd respondent had no reasonable suspicion against the petitioner at the time of arrest. The report and statements did not implicate the petitioner in unlawful activity under the PTA. Therefore, the arrest was unlawful and violated Article 13(1).
principles_established: Arrest must be based on reasonable suspicion supported by credible information.
Arrest under PTA section 6(1) must comply with constitutional safeguards in Article 13(1).
False or pretended arrests under PTA do not justify detention under PTA provisions.
precedents_cited: Channa Pieris v. A. G. (1994) 1 Sri LR 1

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s arrest was not in accordance with law under Article 13(1) and was unlawful.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(1) protects against unlawful arrest and requires informing the arrested person of the reason. The court’s reasoning and holding directly address the legality of the petitioner’s arrest under this clause.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found no reasonable suspicion existed for the petitioner’s arrest under section 6(1) of the PTA and that the petitioner was likely informed of the reason for arrest but the arrest was unlawful.
